hints: Kotivalo and Justiina cannot read the same book simultaneously, so each book's time contributes to one person's work.
The total time must be at least the sum of all reading times.
If the longest book exceeds the time spent on all other books, it forces that book to finish after the others; otherwise both can keep busy until the total sum.
analogy: Two readers can work in parallel, except one especially long book may dominate the schedule.
example: Times 2,8,3 sum to 13; the longest is 8, so the minimum is max(13,2*8)=16.
algorithm: Compute total S and maximum M. Print max(S,2*M).
correctness: No schedule can finish before total work S or before the reader of the longest book completes it after the other reader's workload; this lower bound is attainable by dividing the remaining books between the two readers.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
